clarity.justification: The plan closely addresses the topic and gives directional, decidable predictions, including that a compact "k<=10" head set should reach "AUROC >=0.75 held-out and >=0.70 across paraphrases," while "AUROC <=0.60 or no better than the random-head control" refutes the compact-router claim. It also specifies what is varied and measured through attention-head, MLP, residual, random-source, and intervention comparisons, with explicit positive, undecidable, and negative bands. However, Experiment 2 patches "per-head attention output from the expressed run into the hidden run" between pairs merely "matched on relation and popularity decile"; because an attention-head output carries content as well as routing information, a successful patch would not cleanly establish that routing rather than transferred content caused the flip, and the attention-versus-MLP flip ratio may not compare equivalent interventions. The broader wording "if routing proves diffuse we report a distributed gate rather than abandon the account" weakens falsifiability of the general gating narrative, although the primary compact-head and intervention claims remain clearly refutable.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is the proposed "activation patching ... of the residual stream, per-layer MLP output, and per-head attention output" across matched runs; this requires substantial custom experiment logic but is a standard operation supported by forward hooks and established causal-tracing/activation-patching tooling rather than an undefined magic step. The named models and datasets—"Llama-3-8B," "GPT-J-6B," "Qwen3-8B," PopQA, LAMA/T-REx, and EntityQuestions—and methods such as logistic probes and ROME exist, while attention scaling, nested logistic regression, and perplexity evaluation are implementable with standard ML libraries. Resources are unusually concrete, including "12,000 facts," "1,500 pairs," "5 paraphrases per fact," "800" intervention cases, explicit seeds, head-set sizes, and collateral evaluations on "100 matched unrelated facts." The refuting branch is runnable because the design includes random-label, shuffled-activation, random-source, random-head, MLP, all-head, prompt-engineering, and unsupported-fact controls, although the cross-fact patching confound limits what a negative or positive patching result can establish mechanistically rather than preventing execution.
